 Jazz coach gets honest if they regret letting Walker Kessler leave for Lakers 
 2026-11-19 04:10 
 Will Hardy would rather focus on his current Utah Jazz group than dwell on the possibilities of what could have happened if they had kept Walker Kessler instead of letting him join the Lakers.
 Credit: ZUMA Press-Scanpix 
 Credit ZUMA Press-Scanpix 
 Credit ZUMA Press-Scanpix 
 Add us on 
 Add us on 
 Utah Jazz head coach Will Hardy believes there is no point in dwelling on "what-ifs" or regretting whether they could have retained Walker Kessler instead of letting the big man join the Los Angeles Lakers.
 Walker Kessler 
 Los Angeles Lakers 
 Position 
 C

 25

 Birth place

 Profile 
 Statistics 
 While Hardy emphasized that he still strongly values the bond he built with Kessler during their four years together in Utah, the Jazz coach would rather focus and put his commitment on the new group around him.
 "That is a part of our league. You know, I value my relationship with him and all the experiences that we went through together," Hardy told reporters ahead of the Jazz's Wednesday face-off against Kessler and the Lakers. "Lauri [Markkanen] is now the only player that was on our team at the beginning of the time that I was here and Walker would have been the other one. So there was a longstanding relationship there. Ultimately, I'm happy for Walker, the human being, because we do have a real relationship and he's, you know, a wonderful guy.
 "As far as like thinking about him being with us, you know, those are just sort of dangerous places to get into because you start going down an unproductive road. You know, this is our group, that's who we're focused on helping."
 Walker Kessler leaves Utah Jazz, joins LA Lakers as restricted free agent
 Walker Kessler left the Utah Jazz in 2026 free agency, as the LA Lakers notably acquired the big man by sending out unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 alongside first-round draft pick swaps in 2028 and 2030.
 As part of the sign-and-trade deal, Kessler agreed to a four-year, $130 million contract with Los Angeles.
 Even before free agency began, reports surfaced about Kessler's complicated contract situation with the Jazz, with the big man reportedly growing frustrated with how the franchise handled his restricted free agency.

 In the end, despite making it clear that he wants to stay in Salt Lake City, Kessler reportedly threatened the Jazz by possibly exercising his qualifying offer and entering the 2027 offseason as an unrestricted free agent, which would have let Utah lose him for nothing.
 So far, Kessler is enjoying his new beginnings with the Lakers, averaging 14.5 points, 10.9 rebounds, and 1.9 assists per game on a league-leading 68.0% shooting to anchor their NBA-best 13-2 start.
 The Jazz, on the other hand, stumbled in disappointments amid the injuries of Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) and Lauri Markkanen (hand), holding a 2-13 record entering the Wednesday game.
 "I always want the guys that we have to do well," Hardy added. "You know, tonight we're competing against him, but yeah, I think the nature of our business is it's always been that way.
 "It feels like it's getting more and more, but I think it's something that we all adjust to."
